problem:
The $3$rd term of a geometric sequence is $5$, and the $6$th term is $40.$ What is the first term of this sequence to exceed
$2\,020?$

feedback.problem: The $6$th term of a geometric sequence is $972$, and the common ratio is $3.$ The first term of this sequence to exceed $30\,000$ is the{{field-1}}th term.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we are given that ${a}_{6}=972$ and  $r=3$, we can use the $n$th term formula to solve for ${a}_{1}$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\ {a}_{6} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{6-1} \\ 972 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{5} \\ 972 & =243{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{972}{243} \\ {a}_{1} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $n$th term of the geometric sequence is

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =4\cdot {3}^{n-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want $n$th term to be greater than $30\,000.$
Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot {3}^{n-1} & >30\,000 \\ {3}^{n-1} & >7\,500 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({3}^{n-1}) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(7\,500) \\ (n-1)\operatorname{log}⁡(3) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(7\,500) \\ n-1 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(7\,500)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(7\,500)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(7\,500)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}+1≈9.122.
$$

Therefore, the $10$th term is the first term of the sequence that exceeds $30\,000.$
